The marker fixes the region's **interface** (TDL-1, §10).
The body is partitioned by content (§10) and never rejected for containing classical code; the plugin outlines coherent slices of action bodies (TDL-3).

An **oracle region** is a lifted classical oracle with output targets and a fault register (ISA §5.2); an **action region** is a quantum action on the wires its events name (ISA §5.3) with no fault outcome of its own: a fault of an oracle it calls lands in a fault register the action declares (§10, TDL-8).
The candidate set RR(v) of a region operand v is computed from its abstract value (§5):
every `FN(F)` atom of AV(v), resolved by `resolve` below;

if AV(v) has the ⊤ flag: in addition every function of the required type of §7.1 (for `oracle`/`inplace`: every function) whose address is used anywhere in the linked program, resolved (decision 3 read literally: "every function whose address can reach a region marker"; audit B-33).
The set is therefore always bounded by the program.

`resolve(F)` follows aliases to their aliasee and **forwarding thunks** to their target: F is a forwarding thunk of G iff F's body is one block holding exactly a call of G (optionally `tail`/`musttail`/`notail`, default calling convention, no operand bundles) whose arguments are F's parameters in order and whose function type equals F's, followed by `ret void` or `ret` of that call's result; then `resolve(F) = resolve(G)`, except that a thunk on a cycle of thunks resolves to itself (it is an ordinary defined function whose execution recurses until a budget or the host stops it; 0.1's `BD-E-REGION-THUNK` is deleted).
**Dispatch.** The region operand is classical data.
The plugin compiles a body for every candidate.

At run time the operand's value is compared, by the compare tree of §14.2 over the sorted keys, with A(S) of every **source** S (every function or alias that resolves into the candidate set and whose address reaches v, plus every candidate itself); on equality the region `resolve(S)` is entered.
No match is the run-time trap `T-REGION` (fault code 4).
A candidate with no definition (an external declaration, a function without bitcode) is entered as a trapped call: F(8) with a coverage line (§4.5 item 4).

**Ill-formed candidates.** A candidate that is not well-formed for the marker's kind (a type other than §7.1's, or a violation of §7.5) is compiled as a **trap body** (`T-REGION-INVALID`, fault code 4) with a coverage line: it may never be dispatched, so it is not a compile-time error.
It is rejected (`BD-E-REGION-TYPE`, `BD-E-REGION-MEASURE`, `BD-E-REVERSIBLE-MEASURE`) only when it is the **unique** candidate, because then every execution of the marker fails (outline E14).
0.1's `BD-E-REGION-UNBOUNDED` and `BD-E-REGION-EXTERNAL` are deleted.
A region is identified by its content, never by its symbol.
Candidates that resolve to the same function are one region.

The semantic identity of an **oracle region** in a shape (§8.4) is the interface hash (ISA §9.2) of `@ref` in its reference object (§16.2): every lproc, data image and layout leaf of the closure is part of it, and `@ref`, `@L<n>`, `@G<n>` are fixed names, so two functions with equal materialised bodies have equal identity whatever their source names.
Symbol names, linkage, aliases and thunks are non-normative: diagnostics and coverage entries MAY print them.
Budget lookup uses the separate provisional `selection_identity` and the once-only staging of §9.2, never a fixed point in this final semantic identity.

The **region key** of any region is the SHA-256 of the text printed by the LLVM printer of the major in use for a module that contains the materialised region function and its closure, after `strip` (local names), with the functions renamed `f0, f1, …` in depth-first preorder from the region along direct calls in instruction order, and without datalayout, triple and module metadata.
It keys the budget table (§9.2) and is recorded in the certificate and coverage entries.
It depends on the LLVM major, which the certificate records (§24, D13).
NS §4.2: "the plugin classifies each outlined region by its contents and the verifier checks the declared interface".
After the TDL partition (§10):

an action region whose generated events are all permutation events (X-family gates, `qload`, `qstore`, `qexch`, oracle calls, permutation actions) is emitted as an ISA `perm_action` (ISA §5.3), which certificates can verify by T3; otherwise as an `action`;
an oracle region stays an oracle;

a `reversible` marker call reached from an action region's generation or from an L closure is not an R entry: its operand is treated as a direct call of the region function, partitioned by TDL inside actions and lifted inside oracles, with the call's budget record governing its slices (§9.3; audit B-37).
0.1's `BD-E-REGION-TIER` and `T-TIER` are deleted.
Only the rules the north star requires:

**(a) Measurement in a unitary region.** A `measure` call in the closure of an action region is `BD-E-REGION-MEASURE` (NS §3.1: "user measurement inside it is refused"), unless the module requests **deferred measurement** with the module flag `!{i32 1, !"bennett.measure_in_unitary", !"defer"}` (NS §3.1: "or, when the front end asks for it, deferred by the deferred-measurement principle, which the certificate states").
Then a `measure(h, i)` inside a generation becomes a `qcopy` of `h.i` onto a fresh wire w (ISA §4.5), the call's `i1` result is a Co value whose wire is w (§10, TDL-2 seed).
Retain this intentional outcome record until the first permitted CC measurement boundary after the outermost action returns, and measure it there before the next source operation.
Earlier removal requires the complete instrument (outcomes and correlations included) to be unchanged; an open window alone never justifies quncopy.
These channel outputs are separate from clean workspace (TDL-7).
Standalone adj uses the deterministic latest-before-reversed-consumer placement of §18.2, including source-wire lifetime extension.

The coverage report has a `lowered` entry with source `dialect-0.2.10:7.5a` for every such call, and the certificate lists the id `deferred_measurement` in the region's `definedness_assumptions` (ISA §12.3; §25.2 records the wording item).

**(b) Reversible regions.** The closure of a reversible region MAY contain gate and region markers on handles received through `env`: they lower to R-tier `action_call`/`oracle_call` (ISA §3.1, §4.7), recorded in the R history and reversed by re-application or adjoint (ISA §7.4).
A `measure` call in the closure is `BD-E-REVERSIBLE-MEASURE` (ISA §10: a run that measured is not reversible; ISA §3.3: a `measure` frame is never reversed).

A `qalloc`, `qborrow` or `qfree` in the closure is **hoisted** (ISA 0.8 has `qreg.new` in CC only): when every such site s has a finite reference instance bound N(s) (§6.5 rules 1 and 2, applied to every site whether or not it reaches memory, including the entry-boundary liveness precondition with the reversible invocation in place of the device entry), the CC caller allocates N(s) clean registers per site before the R call, passes them as `qreg` arguments, and frees them after it returns; `qalloc` in R selects a free one, `qfree` checks that it is clean (`T-CLEAN`) and returns it to the free set.
Otherwise the site is a blocker point of BLK-4 (`blocked:BD-B-ISA12`, §25.1).
**(c) In-place pairs** are verified by §8.7.
Deferred measurement is a channel on adjoint paths as well: the special §18.2 rule creates fresh retained records for standalone adj and retains E_f records through compute.
An open window never authorises quncopy of these records.

The plugin additionally outlines coherent slices (TDL-3), which is not observable beyond §18.

`env` points to classical memory the front end owns (an `alloca` or heap object) that is live for the duration of the marker call; the region reads and writes it as classical memory (§18.4).
Handles reach a region through `env` (PT9 binds a region's parameter to the marker's env argument).
Oracle regions are arbitrary functions bound by a descriptor (§8); no packing wrapper is needed (audit D21).
A region body MUST be referenced by the region operand (directly or through §7.2); a body referenced only from a side-table global is not a region (enzyme survey implication 5).
Region functions SHOULD have internal linkage, so that they are not device entries.

`__bennett_oracle(f, budget, desc)` applies the lifted oracle of region function f, under the budget of §9, to the registers and classical values that the **descriptor** `desc` binds to f's parameters, result and device models.
`__bennett_inplace(g, ginv, budget, desc)` applies an in-place bijection (§8.7).
The descriptor is classical data in the caller's memory, built by plain stores (§3.8); its kinds are classical values dispatched over their finite domains (§8.4).
The descriptor is the LLVM struct `{ H, [nparam x Bind], [ndev x DevBind] }` laid out by the module's datalayout, where (C view in `bennett_markers.h`, §3.3):
H | `{ i32, i32, i32, i32, ptr, ptr }` | `version` (= 2), `nparam`, `ndev`, `flags` (= 0), `tgt`, `fault`
Bind | `{ i32, i32, ptr, i64, i64 }` | `kind`, `mode`, `q`, `value`, `size`
DevBind | `{ i32, i32, ptr, i64 }` | `model`, `mode` (= 0), `q`, `value`

On x86-64, AArch64 and RISC-V64 (pw = 64) H is 32 bytes, Bind 32 bytes (`kind` at 0, `mode` 4, `q` 8, `value` 16, `size` 24) and DevBind 24 bytes, so `param[i]` is at 32 + 32i and `dev[j]` at 32 + 32·nparam + 24j.
The plugin reads the descriptor at the marker call, in the caller's tier, with ordinary loads.
`nparam` MUST equal the number of flattened scalar fields of the dispatched region function after N21/N22 and ABI lowering, using §8.2 carriers (one field for a scalar).

A descriptor whose `version`, `flags`, `nparam` or any kind, mode or model is not one this section defines, or whose binding does not fit the parameter's type (below), traps (`T-IFACE`, fault code 4) when the marker is called.
Let the dispatched region function have IR parameters p_0 … p_{m−1} and return type R (`void` or a first-class type of at most 128 payload bits after N25, §12.2).
Before binding, represent each floating-point scalar by its §13.1 integer carrier (half/bfloat i16, float i32, double i64, x86_fp80 i80, fp128/ppc_fp128 i128).
IN and ARG bind carrier bits.
Flatten aggregate/vector parameters depth-first in field/lane order, one Bind per scalar field; apply N21/N22 first.
`param[i]` binds flattened field i.
Results concatenate fields in the same order, field 0 in the lowest bits, no padding; width is the sum of scalar carrier widths.
N25 demotes results whose packed width exceeds 128 bits.
Memory accesses retain datalayout padding; this padding is never part of the packed return payload:

`IN` | 1 | `iW` or `ptr addrspace(a)` (W = P(a)) | q with n(q) ≤ W | the parameter's value is the basis value of q, zero-extended (`mode` = ZEXT 0) or sign-extended (`mode` = SEXT 1) to W; a `ptr` parameter may be `IN` (a superposed pointer) | an `ins` bundle `x<k>:wire[n(q)]` (a pseudo-location, ISA §3.7), extended by `lift.zext`/`lift.sext` in the wrapper

`ARG` | 2 | `iW` (W ≤ 128) or `ptr` | none (`q` ignored) | a classical value: bits 0–63 from `value`, bits 64–127 from `size`; a `ptr` ARG is an address in the caller's classical memory, which the oracle reads through its entry state (§8.5) | an `args` entry `a<k>:i<W>` (W = P(a) for `ptr addrspace(a)`; ISA §4.7, §5.1)

`MEM_IN` | 3 | `ptr` | q with n(q) = 8·2^A, `size` = 2^A | the parameter is the base address of an interface region of 2^A bytes whose cell i is byte i of q (bits [8i, 8i + 8)); its contents may be superposed; role `in` (restored on every basis configuration, ISA §5.1).
This is the quantum-addressed memory of NS §8 rung 4 | a `mem` region `m<k>:region[A,8] in`; the argument is `lift.addr @m<k>`

`OUT` | 4 | `ptr` | q with n(q) = 8·`size` | the parameter points to a fresh zero-filled buffer of `size` bytes in the oracle's memory; at exit its final bytes are XORed into q, byte k into wires [8k, 8k + 8) (a declared output, NS §4.2) | `lift.alloc size` in the wrapper; the bytes are part of the payload (§8.6)
`INOUT` | 5 | `iW` | q with n(q) = W | `inplace` only (§8.7): the in-place register x | `qinplace … x`

The **result**: a non-null `tgt` register receives the return value: payload bits = the return value zero-extended to n(tgt) if n(tgt) ≥ R's width; if n(tgt) is narrower, the dropped bits are checked and an execution on which they are nonzero faults with code 4 (`FAULT_UB_TRAP`); the retained bits are the low n(tgt).
A null `tgt` discards the return value.
For `oracle`, the **fault register** `fault` MUST be a register of exactly 4 wires (ISA §5.4: F = 4) and MUST NOT be null (`T-IFACE`).
Null `tgt` remains valid for a `void` function or a discarded non-void return.
If there is no `OUT` or non-null `CONSOLE` output either, the shape has zero payload outputs; it still executes once and delivers its fault through §8.6's synthetic variant.
Every register named by the descriptor MUST be live and pairwise distinct (`T-DEAD`, `T-ALIAS`).
A width mismatch in the table above is `T-SIZE`.
`dev[j]` binds a device model for the lifted (coherent) tier (§11.3):

statements.text: `ENTROPY` | 1 | q with n(q) = 8·2^A | an `in` region `e0:region[A,8]` holding the entropy tape, possibly superposed (NS §8 rung 8: "the entropy device is replaced by a superposed register")
`BLOCK` | 2 | q with n(q) = 8·512·2^A′ | an `in` region `k0` holding the disk image of 2^A′ sectors; writes go to a lifted copy-on-write overlay in the oracle's heap
`CLOCK` | 3 | none | the clock model's initial value is `value`

`CONSOLE` | 4 | q with n(q) = 8·L, or null | the first L bytes the oracle writes to the console are XORed into q as an output (payload, §8.6); with a null q console bytes are discarded with the oracle's other writes
At most one binding per model.

statements.text: A model without a binding is **unbound**: an effect on it in L code faults with code 8 on the executions that reach it (§11.3; NS §4.2).
A **shape** is the tuple (region candidate F; for each parameter its kind, mode, register width n(q) and `size`; n(tgt) or "none"; for each device binding its model and n(q)).
The kind, mode, model, `size` and `value` fields have value sets (§5.3); register widths come from the register file (§6.5), whose roots have known widths.

The plugin compiles one reference object (§16.2) per shape that the value sets allow, taking every unbounded kind or mode field over its finite domain (5 kinds, 2 modes, 4 models), so the number of shapes is always bounded.

At run time the caller's tier reads the descriptor and selects the compiled shape with the compare tree of §14.2; a descriptor that matches no compiled shape traps (`T-IFACE`), which happens only for a field outside its table.
`value` and `size` of `ARG` bindings are the oracle's classical arguments and are not part of the shape.
*(non-normative)* With one valid value per shape field there is one shape per candidate.
Initial zero possibilities still participate in §5; kind 0 is outside the five-kind table and takes T-IFACE rather than creating an additional valid shape.

The marker then issues, in the caller's tier, one **oracle invocation** (§8.6) whose operands are the static registers the descriptor's handles denote (§6.5), the budget token (§9.5) and the classical arguments.

**Reference semantics.** The region function runs on a **private copy of the caller's whole classical memory at the call**, with the bound inputs; its writes are discarded except through `OUT`, `tgt` and the bound device outputs (NS §4.2: "every other write being restored workspace").
Constant globals, and mutable globals that only the oracle's own L closure writes, equal their initialisers at every call.
**Realisation on ISA 0.8.** Let R be the abstract objects the oracle closure may load (§5.4), minus constant globals and mutable globals written by no function outside the L closure.
Translate source read-set objects after normalisation to runtime backing allocations.
If R includes a caller alloca/frame, include its live shadow-stack backing storage and metadata, bytes and addresses.
If reachability is uncertain, include all live caller heap/stack backing allocations.
Whenever the L closure uses the shadow stack, add its state globals to G and its block to Hb with current base, size and stack pointer, even without a source heap object.
Include the logical frame/allocation table of §17.3, dynamic extents, liveness and save/restore state in G whenever stack access or stack operations can execute.
Replay these bytes before private allocations/accesses and let ss_init adopt them; a live backing entry alone does not recreate live program frames.
All such metadata mutations invalidate snapshot reuse independently of the byte read set.
Allocator metadata is an independent entry-state dependency: allocation, deallocation, allocation-validity checks and observation of allocation-derived addresses read it even without an LLVM load.
Replay the complete caller allocation history (sizes and live bits) whenever any can execute, including when the byte read set R is empty.
Bytes are included only for byte dependencies; the sound default is the complete table, with a smaller proven dependency optional.
Only when both byte and allocator-state dependencies are absent may transfer be omitted and globals start at their images (ISA §3.7), as in rung 4 route A (SQLite §5.2(i)).
After replay heap_used, atop and stack-state values equal the caller's call-entry values.
Otherwise the plugin emits an **entry-state transfer**:

**Snapshot.** At the call the caller's tier forms the byte string S = k ‖ (size_i ‖ live_i)_{i<k} ‖ G ‖ Hb, where k is an 8-byte little-endian count of heap allocations in the caller's allocation table (in allocation order, ISA §7.1), `size_i` and `live_i` are 8-byte little-endian fields (`live_i` is 0 or 1), G is the bytes of the mutable globals in R in `layout.globals` order, and Hb is the bytes of every live heap allocation in allocation order if R contains a heap object or shadow-stack backing allocation (else empty); each live Hb segment has exactly size_i bytes, even for size_i=0.
S is zero-padded to 2^A_s bytes, where A_s is the smallest exponent with 2^A_s ≥ 8 + 16·N_alloc + Σ|G| + `heap_limit_max` (N_alloc the allocation-table capacity of the layout, §19.5); A_s is static.
The snapshot bytes S are assembled in a plugin-added unnamed CC global of 2^A_s bytes, zero-filled before every build; thus all 16-byte leaf loads, including padding, are valid.

**Register.** The CC tier builds a register of 8·2^A_s wires holding S with a **concat tree** of A_s − 3 static-width CC functions `B_j` (j = 4, …, A_s): `B_4(p)` executes `qreg.new any 128`, loads the 16 bytes at p as two `i64` values and makes the `oracle_call` of the runtime oracle `@xor128` (§16.5) that XORs them into the register (with a token minted at launch for budget (6, 0, 0, 0) and a fresh 4-wire fault register, which stays clean and is freed); `B_j(p)` (j > 4) returns `qreg.concat B_{j−1}(p) B_{j−1}(p + 2^{j−1})`.
Every type is static and the cost is 2^(A_s−4) region calls.
The register is bound as an extra `in` region `s0:region[A_s,8]`.

**Replay.** The wrapper prologue (§16.2) calls the runtimes function `__bennett_rt_entry_replay(s0)`, which for i < k executes `__bennett_nz_alloc(size_i)` (ISA `lift.alloc`) and, if `live_i` = 0, `__bennett_nz_free` of the result.
ISA §4.2 `lift.alloc` and ISA §7.1 `alloc` share the rule "bump + max(n, 1) from `heap_base`", so the replay reproduces the caller's heap addresses exactly (audit O-07).
It then copies G into the globals (by the driver-generated table `__bennett_rt_entry_table` of their addresses and sizes) and Hb into the replayed live allocations.
**Release.** The snapshot register holds the basis state |S⟩ and is unentangled after every oracle call (an `in` region is unchanged on every basis configuration, ISA §5.2).
The caller keeps it for later calls only while its dependent bytes and allocator metadata are unchanged.

Relevant alloc/free and shadow-stack push/pop/restore invalidate it as well as stores to R, and releases it by unpreparation: retain the classical S for the register's lifetime, take successive slice views of at most 128 bits, invoke the same @xor128 preparation oracle with the original two i64 arguments on each 128-bit chunk (one view per call), then qreg.free the now-clean whole register.
A_s ≥ 4, so every leaf is exactly 128 bits.
No whole-register measurement, view measurement or un-concat operation is needed.
The replay's rows, allocations and calls are part of the reference body and count against the budget (§9.4).
Entry-state transfer from R-tier code needs registers allocated in R (BLK-4, §25.1); no rung uses it.
**Build-time snapshots** (rung 7, §19.6) rewrite the initialisers of the mutable globals to snapshot values at link time, so byte transfer may be empty; allocator dependencies still require replay.
Efficiency: G-12 (§25.3).
The **outputs** of a shape are, in order: `tgt` (if non-null), each `OUT` parameter in parameter order, and the `CONSOLE` register (if bound and non-null).
Each output register is split into **slices** of at most 128 bits from its low end (ISA §3.3: payloads are `iN` with N ≤ 128); the slices of all outputs are numbered 0, 1, …, k − 1 in that order.
Every slice j has an oracle **variant** W_j: the same reference body (§16.2) whose `lift.retval` delivers slice j of the payload.
Every W_j executes an identical ordered computation and validation of every projection, with identical row charges and fault conditions; only its last lift.retval operand differs.
Thus all variants compute the same fault code, even when budget expires in delivery, and all copy-outs are zero on any common failure.
For a single slice, retain its existing rows and return directly without an extra projection move.
**k = 0** (no payload outputs): there is one synthetic variant **W_empty**, with T = 1.
It executes the same prologue, region body and unwind check as other variants; on success its terminal rows are `p0 = lift.const.i1 0` and `lift.retval p0` (§16.2), charged normally.

The caller allocates one clean hidden target bit, invokes `oracle_call @W_empty tk (ins..) hidden fault (mem..) (args..)` exactly once using the caller's required four-wire fault register, then frees the hidden target.
The hidden bit remains zero on success and fault; it is workspace, not a payload output.
Under invocation controls, predicate the call on all of them; allocation and free remain unconditional.
Do not issue a second call to clean the hidden target: that would XOR away the delivered fault code.
**k = 1** (every output fits 128 bits in one register): the invocation is `oracle_call @W_0 tk (ins..) tgt fault (mem..) (args..)`.
**k > 1** (the `wide` event, §18.2): the caller's tier issues, for j = k − 1, …, 1, with slice j at bits [lo_j, lo_j + w_j) of output register o_j:

```
  t_j = qreg.new any w_j ; f_j = qreg.new any 4
  oracle_call @W_j tk (ins..) t_j f_j (mem..) (args..)
  s_j = qreg.slice o_j lo_j w_j
  action_call @xor<w_j> (s_j) (t_j) () ()
  oracle_call @W_j tk (ins..) t_j f_j (mem..) (args..)
  qreg.free f_j ; qreg.free t_j
  ```
followed by `s_0 = qreg.slice o_0 lo_0 w_0` and `oracle_call @W_0 tk (ins..) s_0 fault (mem..) (args..)`.

statements.text: `@xor<w>` is the permutation action `(mut s:wire[w]) (in t:wire[w]) () ()` with body `qxor t s`; each slice view is the operand of exactly one region call (ISA §3.3).

Each copy-out pair computes slice j into fresh wires, XORs it into the target and uncomputes it by the identical self-adjoint call, whose inputs no call in between modifies, so `t_j` and `f_j` are clean when freed (ISA §5.2 involution; the ISA §3.3 cleanliness check of `qreg.free`); slice 0 and the fault code are delivered by the last call.
The effect is exactly NS's F_B with a wide payload: slice_j ⊕= payload_j(F_B(x)) for every j and fault ⊕= code(F_B(x)).
Cost: 2k − 1 oracle calls (efficiency item G-15, §25.3).
Under a `ctrl` every region call is `ctl`-prefixed (§18.2).

`inplace(g, ginv, budget, desc)` binds the in-place register x as `INOUT` (exactly one parameter of each candidate pair is `INOUT`, of type `iN` with N = n(x); the result type is `iN`). g and ginv are oracles in the sense of §8.2 with a **payload equal to the new value of x**: their reference objects (§16.2) bind x as an `in` bundle and have an n(x)-bit target.

The descriptor's `tgt` MUST be null and its `fault` is ignored (`T-IFACE` otherwise): an in-place update has no fault outcome (NS §4.2), and the `qinplace` expansion allocates its own clean scratch (ISA §4.5).
**No other bindings**: the call lowers to ISA `qinplace @g @ginv tk x` (ISA §4.5) with @g, @ginv the reference oracles of the pair.

**Classical `ARG`s with finite value sets**: one `qinplace` per tuple of argument values, each with the pair specialised to those constants (the arguments become `lift.const` in the reference bodies), dispatched by §14.2.

**Library bijections**: when the pair is a `bennett-arith` library bijection (add or subtract a value, xor, rotate, negate, byte swap, modular addition, modular multiplication by a unit, each with its stated conditions and its g∘ginv = id certificate, NS §3.1), the call lowers to the library's permutation action with `IN`, `MEM_IN` and `ARG` bindings as its `in`, `mem` and `args` operands, which ISA 0.8 expresses directly (ISA §4.7 `action_call`).
This is also the TDL-5(b) mechanism (§10).
**User pairs with `IN`, `MEM_IN` or arbitrary `ARG`s**: allocate clean n(x)-wire t and 4-wire f at the CC boundary.
Issue oracle_call @g tk (x, ins..) t f (mem..) (args..), exchange x and t by a swap action, then oracle_call @ginv tk (x, ins..) t f (mem..) (args..), and qreg.free t and f.
Preserved parameter bindings are identical in both calls.
Under control, predicate every region call including the swap; allocation/free remain unconditional.
This is a CC-level expansion like §8.6, not an assertion that a static action passes ISA §6's coarse provenance windows.
Universal inverse and fault-free budget obligations below guarantee clean scratch on every basis state, hence on superpositions.
Parameterised qinplace is efficiency only (§25.3); BLK-3 is retired.

**Verification.** For every compiled pair and every argument tuple, when N ≤ the configured width (driver option `-bennett-inplace-exhaustive-bits`, default 24, §24), the plugin MUST run the reference interpreter on both reference bodies with an unbounded budget and check that for every x ∈ [0, 2^N), F^g(x) = (y, 0) and F^ginv(y) = (x, 0); it records the **minimal budget** B_min, the componentwise maximum over all those runs of (rows, heap bytes, stack cells, depth).

Above that width it MUST record a `sampled` evidence claim (ISA §12.1) of the same check and B_sample over the sample as an observed lower bound only, and the dynamic net applies: a wrong inverse leaves the scratch register of the `qinplace` expansion non-clean, which `T-CLEAN` catches (NS §3.1).

F_B is monotone in the budget (a run that completes within B completes identically within every B′ ≥ B), so the pair is valid for exactly B ≥ B_min only when the check is exhaustive over the full input/parameter domain.
Sampling cannot establish B_min or universal invertibility.
In all sampled cases validity assumes mutually inverse total functions and a sound bound B_bound covering every input and parameter value.
A library or producer-supplied bound is permitted with an explicit correctness obligation recorded in the certificate; no mechanised proof format is required.
B_sample never substitutes for B_bound, and T-CLEAN is not a universal budget guarantee.
Use B_bound in the following budget checks for sampled pairs.

A pair that fails the check, or whose budget is static and below B_min in some component, is `BD-E-INPLACE-NOT-INVERSE` (NS §3.1: "an in-place update with no inverse fails loud at compile time"; "a fallible or budget-limited computation cannot be in-place"); a run-time budget (§9.5) below B_min traps at the marker (`T-BUDGET`).
*(non-normative)* On a finite set, ginv∘g = id makes g injective, hence a bijection, so g∘ginv = id and ginv is fault-free on every input, as ISA `qinplace` requires.
0.1's `BD-E-INPLACE-UNVERIFIED` is deleted.
**Zero payload outputs (round 3).** With no payload slices, success still runs four charged rows: call, void return, zero constant, retval.
Budget 3 therefore faults 1; budget 4 succeeds.
Explicit fault 4 exits before delivery, but still reaches the caller's fault register.
A discarded non-void result is not a hidden payload or a dropped-bit check.
The caller witness executes one call and a real clean hidden-target free on success, fault and zero budget; basis controls 0/1 respectively suppress/preserve fault delivery.
It never cleans by calling twice.
The marker form has null `tgt`, zero parameter bindings and a live four-wire fault register; it remains accepted:

NS §3.1: a region-level classical budget of "dynamic steps, heap bytes and recursion depth, passed as ordinary integer operands of the region-entry marker or supplied out of band by the host or driver (a project-wide default, a per-function table) … No per-loop source annotation is ever required".
Budgets are the ISA's four components (ISA §5.4).
Every region-entry marker takes a `ptr` to a **budget record** (outline E1, E12), the LLVM struct `{ i64, i64, i64, i64, ptr }` under the datalayout (C `bennett_budget`, §3.3):
`steps` | B: reference-interpreter rows (§9.4)
`heap` | `heap_limit`: heap bytes (ISA §5.4)
`stack` | `stack_limit`: lifted stack cells (ISA §3.7)
`depth` | `depth_limit`: call depth
`fault` | action regions only: the caller's fault register (4 wires) that receives the combined fault of the region's coherent slices (§10, TDL-8), or null
A field equal to `BENNETT_BUDGET_TABLE` (all ones) takes its value from the budget table (§9.2).
A null record means all four budget fields come from the table and `fault` is null.
For `oracle` and `inplace` the `fault` field is ignored: the descriptor names the fault register (§8.2).
The budget-table JSON schema version remains 0.2; it is separate from full dialect 0.2.10.
The **budget table** is a driver input (`--bennett-budgets=<file>`), one JSON document in RFC 8785 canonical form:

```
{ "version": "0.2",
  "defaults": { "steps": D, "heap": D, "stack": D, "depth": D, "sstack": D },
  "entries": [ { ("identity": HEX64 | "region_key": HEX64 | "symbol": GLOB),
                 "steps"?: D, "heap"?: D, "stack"?: D, "depth"?: D, "sstack"?: D } … ] }
```
with D a decimal string.
statements.uncertain: no RFC keyword, defined term, example marker or declarative verb

statements.text: Selectors are `identity` (a provisional shape interface hash, **selection_identity**, defined below), `region_key` (§7.3), or a source-symbol glob (`*` and `?`).
Resolution is staged and MUST NOT seek a fixed point:

Resolve baseline values per region, shape and component, ignoring identity entries: the first matching region-key entry naming that component, else the first matching symbol entry naming it, else the default.
Missing defaults come from `--bennett-budget-default=<s,h,st,d,ss>`, then 1048576 steps, 1048576 heap bytes, 65536 stack cells, depth 256 and `sstack` 65536 (§24).
`sstack` is shadow-stack bytes (§17.3), part of the heap budget.

Freeze the link's layout capacities (§16.3) using componentwise maxima of all effective defaults, every raw table entry (including unmatched identity entries), and non-sentinel statically supplied budget fields (the all-ones sentinel is a lookup request, not a capacity).
Neither lookup nor final-object generation shrinks or recomputes these capacities.
Construct each shape's provisional reference object under that frozen layout, with baseline `sstack` and other baseline wrapper inputs.
Its interface hash is `selection_identity`.
For each component overlay the first identity entry naming that component whose selector equals `selection_identity`, else keep its baseline value.
Apply this overlay **once only**.
Generate the final object using the resolved values; its hash is the semantic identity of §7.3.
Never rematch against this final hash.
Explicit marker-record fields and table sentinels retain §9.1/§9.5 precedence: only table-sourced components use this lookup; non-sentinel explicit fields stay explicit.
Provisionally and finally, the same explicit fields are applied after table lookup.
The resolved table and build record (§19.9) record per shape both `selection_identity` and final `identity`, the resolved components, frozen capacities and the resolved-table SHA-256.
Launch tokens bind the **final** object identity and resolved budget tuple, never the provisional hash.
A steps-only overlay leaves the object hash unchanged but changes its token.
Multiple shapes resolve separately.
*(non-normative)* This is the budget table of the reduced rung-4 link of §16.7: the entry names the region function `q` by symbol; the defaults govern every other region of that link.

Its largest heap (0) and stack (1024) fix that link's `heap_limit_max` and `S_cells` (§16.3); the entry's 400 steps, 512 cells and depth 8 cover the 112 steps, 126 cells and depth 4 that the runs of §16.7 need.
**Staged identity witness (`budget-stage`).** At O0 the 24-byte alloca survives on LLVM 18 and 23.
N24 emits one 24-byte frame; with its 8-byte saved-sp header, the linked runtime below needs 32 bytes.
With all layout inputs fixed, baseline sstack=16 gives H16; an entry keyed by H16 supplies 32 once, producing H32.
Reapplying that entry to H32 would choose 16 and is forbidden.
The linked helper fixture below fixes the runtime/link input for this example (one valid frame, no other shadow-frame users); it is not a replacement specification of the runtimes.
The source pair is N24's canonical output; `budget-stage-runtime` appends those fixed helper definitions before mapping.
The checked state pins both hashes, resolved fields, final wrapper and final-object token outcomes.

statements.text: Everything else is inferred"; NS §3.1 taint row: a context-sensitive interprocedural analysis "over data dependence, control dependence and memory effects, from marker results and region entries … with polyvariant specialisation".
This section replaces 0.1's generation-only semantics, in which classical stores of a `ctrl` body happened on both branches of the control (audit 1.4-d, R1).
Rule ids TDL-1 to TDL-12 are normative anchors.
ISA 0.8 expresses every construct below: actions call oracles (ISA §5.3, §4.7) and CC issues controlled region calls (ISA §4.7 `ctl w <call>`).
**TDL-1 Interface vs body.** The marker fixes the interface: `ctrl`, `adj` and `compute` give an action; `oracle` and `inplace` give an oracle.
The body of an action region is partitioned by content (TDL-3) and is never rejected for containing classical code.
**TDL-2 Coherence states.**

**Object state.** Every instance of an abstract object X has a dynamic state K(X) ∈ {Cl, M, Co}, kept by the CC tier (a runtimes table for globals, the coherent allocator's bookkeeping for heap objects; §11, §17): Cl (the CC **shadow** holds X's bytes; X's arena cells are |0⟩), M (materialised: the arena cells hold the same bytes as a basis state; both are valid), Co (the arena is the truth and may be superposed; the shadow is invalid).
Every instance starts Cl.

Transitions: Cl → M by **materialisation** (an uncontrolled XOR of the shadow into the arena cells, TDL-4); M → Cl by the same XOR (dematerialisation, before a CC store to X); M or Cl → Co when an event is applied (§18.2) that writes X's cells with a non-empty control set or with a Co value; Co → Cl by `__bennett_observe` of all of X's bytes (TDL-11); partial observe leaves K=Co and the observed cells in their measured basis state.
Coverage is tracked since each byte's last write; writes invalidate coverage except a permitted TDL-11 CC store to already-covered bytes.
That store writes a known classical value to both arena and shadow, so the bytes remain covered with that store as their covering write.
Release never changes Co to Cl by fiat: first restore the cells to the basis value equal to the shadow with the invocation's own events, then dematerialise to Cl and release.
Otherwise release traps T-TAINT-HOST (code 4), inside or outside generation, before reuse.

**Value state.** During a generation (§18.4) every executed SSA value instance is Cl or Co: Co iff it is a deferred measurement result (§7.5a), a load of a byte whose **view** (below) is Co, the result of an instruction with a Co operand, or a `phi` at the join of a Co branch.

**View.** A generation sees outliving memory through a **view**: a byte of object X has view Co if K(X) = Co, or if the generation's recorder (or a recorder of an enclosing generation of the same invocation) holds an event that writes it with a non-empty control set or with a Co value; otherwise its view is Cl.

A child generation inherits the invoking generation's current speculative view: apply visible enclosing recorders' classical updates in execution order, then the child's updates, to the invocation-entry shadow.
The enclosing invocation control is added only at event composition, not to this inherited view.
This applies to nested ctrl, adj and compute; sibling arm recorders stay isolated until join.
For `compute`, retain gen(f)'s recorder after it ends: it is visible to gen(use) and adjoint(E_f) construction as part of the same invocation.
Its classical events update use's Cl view; its predicated or Co-valued writes give use a Co view.

*(non-normative)* Inside `ctrl(q, f)` the body's own stores are recorded without q (q is added when the generation ends, TDL-6), so f sees its own writes classically, as the q = 1 branch must; an inner `ctrl(q2, g)` records g's writes with q2, so f's later reads of them are Co.

**Static may-Co analysis MC** (decides partitions, arena placement and the verdict rules below; flow-sensitive, interprocedural over the CC call graph with one summary per (function, coherence signature), merge by union, least fixpoint):
MC1: the state at a program point is the set of abstract objects that may have K = Co there;

MC2: after an action region invocation (`ctrl`, `adj`, `compute`, or a `reversible` call reached from a generation, §7.4), add every outliving object (TDL-5) that a store in the closure of a candidate may write, if the invocation is `ctrl` or the store may be under an inner control, may store a may-Co value, or may be control-dependent on a may-Co branch;
MC3: `__bennett_observe(p, len)` removes an object X when AV(p) = {(X, 0)} and len is a constant ≥ size(X); otherwise no change;
MC4: an instruction is may-Co if an operand may be Co, it is a load whose AV(p) contains a may-Co object, or it is control-dependent on a may-Co branch (stores and calls included).
A value is may-Co if its instruction is; an object written by a may-Co store is may-Co after the store;
MC5: calls bind the coherence signature of the callee (which parameters may be Co, and the may-Co set at entry); every distinct signature is a variant (§4.3).
**Interprocedural and context-sensitive** by coherence signature (MC5; NS §3.1).
**TDL-3 Partition.** For each variant of an action region and of its CC callees:
**G (generation)**: the instructions MC does not mark may-Co.
G runs in CC, once per invocation (§18.4).

**Slices**: every maximal single-entry single-exit region of may-Co instructions other than stores to outliving objects and marker calls is outlined (LLVM `CodeExtractor`) into a **slice function** S_k, with: classical live-ins → `ARG` parameters; Co live-ins → `IN` parameters; may-Co objects it loads → the arena, bound as a `MEM_IN` region `coh`; Co live-outs → outputs (§8.6).
An irreducible may-Co region is outlined as a whole function.
S_k is normalised (§12) and lifted (§16) like any oracle region; its entry state is the generation's view (§8.5: the arena for may-Co objects, the shadow for the rest).
Each slice also keeps its original instructions as a **classical twin** in G.

At run time the generation runs the classical twin when every live-in of the slice is Cl and every object it may load has view Cl; otherwise it records a **slice invocation**: before it, every live instance of a may-Co object the slice may load whose state is Cl is materialised (Cl → M); the invocation computes the Co live-outs into fresh registers (`compute` events, §18.2).
**Stores to outliving objects** and **marker calls** are never inside slices: they become events (TDL-5, TDL-10).
A store or marker call that is control-dependent on a Co branch is recorded under the branch's condition wire (TDL-10).
A Co branch is if-converted: the generation constructs both arms from separate copies of the pre-branch view.
Within each arm its own classical updates are interpreted conditional on that arm being taken; the other arm's recorder is invisible.
Only instructions not control-dependent on the Co branch run classically (none in a plain diamond); all others run in slices or as predicated events.
Views merge only at the join, whose `phi`s become slice-computed selects.
May-Co stores to non-outliving workspace and subsequent dependent reads stay together inside the slice's private memory through the join.
**TDL-4 Coherent arena.**

The objects in any may-Co set of MC are placed in the **arena**: a static address range [A_coh, A_coh + 2^A) of the layout, disjoint from CC globals and heap (ISA §7.1, §7.2; G-13 would lift the restriction).

Globals in the set are relocated into the arena by the layout (§19.5) in both builds, so their addresses stay native-equal; heap objects of may-Co allocation sites are allocated by the runtimes' **coherent allocator** in the arena range in both builds.
The arena's contents are a CC-held register of 8·2^A wires, bound to every slice and arena action as `region[A,8]` (ISA §3.3 binding); cell i is the byte at address A_coh + i.

The **shadow** of the arena is the CC global `__bennett_rt_shadow` of 2^A bytes at A_coh + Δ_sh (a layout constant); CC loads and stores whose abstract address may lie in the arena are rewritten to address + Δ_sh when the object's state is Cl or M, after dematerialising an M object for a store; when the state is Co, TDL-11 applies.

**Writing at a run-time address.** A cell write of a classical mask m at a classical run-time address a (an `xmask` event, a materialisation) lowers to an action that calls the runtime oracle `@xorargs` (§16.5) to XOR the classical `args` (a, m) into fresh wires a_w, m_w, then `qstore coh a_w m_w` (ISA §4.6: XOR into the addressed cell; O(2^A) gates unless the target has QRAM, NS §4.3), then `@xorargs` again to uncompute a_w and m_w.
Objects at static offsets MAY use a static slice (`qreg.slice` with a literal `lo`) and X gates instead.
The physical `coh` interface range is storage, not a logical allocation.
Maintain (base, size, live) for every arena global and coherent heap object.
Before every program memory access of n bytes at p, require the entire nonwrapping [p,p+n) to lie in one live logical allocation.
Otherwise produce fault 7 before access, including event-producing stores, whose mutation is gated on success.
The pinned ISA interface entry never satisfies this additional check.

The default is an ordinary materialised runtime helper `__bennett_rt_coh_check(p,n,table)` over the metadata: visit entries in allocation order, OR their live-and-contained predicates, fault 7 when false, then access.
All helper rows are charged.
A statically proven contained access may omit the helper.
Coherent alloc/free update the same table before subsequent access; snapshot/slice entry transfers metadata along with the corresponding arena view, using preserved `in` metadata for a slice.
Superposed addresses use this same lifted helper, without classical inspection.

**TDL-5 Stores to outliving objects (the store rule).** An object **outlives** an invocation if it is live after it: a global, an object reachable from `env`, or a heap object not freed in the invocation.
A store `store v, ptr p` executed during a generation to an outliving object X is realised by cases on the view of the bytes it writes:
**(a) View Cl** (the old bytes c are known to CC).
v and p Cl: the event `xmask X+o, c ⊕ v` (o = p − X's base).

v or p Co: a slice invocation O computes the address and the mask c ⊕ v into fresh registers (c is a classical argument of O); the event `xstore coh a_w m_w` XORs the mask into the addressed cells (`qstore`); a second identical invocation of O uncomputes the registers.

O never loads X's written bytes from the arena (their view is Cl, so O receives them as arguments), and no instruction between the two invocations writes anything O reads, so the second invocation cleans them exactly (ISA §5.2 involution).
Exact; no history.

**(b) View Co, and the update is a library bijection** in the old value: the materialised IR is `x = load X+o; y = op(x, k…); store y, X+o` with no intervening store to X, where op is one of: add or sub of k (wrapping at the access width), xor with k, rotate by a constant, negate, `bswap`, add of k modulo a constant m (with x < m), multiply by a constant k modulo m with gcd(k, m) = 1 (with x < m); or a declared `inplace` pair (§8.7). k may be Cl or Co (an `IN` binding of a slice output); k MUST NOT depend on X's written bytes.

The event is the `bennett-arith` permutation action for op on the arena cells X+o with k as `in` or `args` (ISA §4.7), preceded by the slice invocation that computes a Co k and followed by its uncomputation.
The complete predicated update MUST be a total bijection on the declared mutable interface, with bounded inverse and clean non-fault workspace.
A bijective op alone is insufficient when its condition depends on the changed bytes.
**(c) View Co, inside the `f` part of `compute(f, use, budget, env)`**: history.

A slice invocation computes the new bytes into a fresh register t; the event `xchg coh a t` exchanges t with the cells (`qexchm`); t now holds the displaced bytes and is kept until adjoint(E_f) replays the events in reverse (`xchg` again, then the slice invocation again), which cleans it (NS §3.1 compute-with-uncompute; Bennett).
`use` MUST NOT write bytes that f wrote by case (c) (`BD-E-COHERENT-OVERWRITE` otherwise: the replay would not restore them).
**(d) Otherwise**: `BD-E-COHERENT-OVERWRITE`, decided statically: a store to an outliving object that MC says may be Co at the store, and that is neither (b) nor (c).
NS §4.2: "writing a register not known to be clean is a compile-time error … an in-place update x ← g(x) requires a total bijection with a bounded inverse … else it fails loud".
The diagnostic names the store and the object.

Stores to objects that do not outlive the invocation are workspace: G runs them on the generation's view only when Cl; may-Co workspace stores and dependent reads run in slices in their private memory (§8.5); at exit the objects are released.
Allocation in a generation is unconditional, like every allocation in the ISA (ISA §3.5); the release of an object that outlives the invocation is TDL-12.
**TDL-6 Control and adjoint.** `ctrl(q, qi, …)` adds wire q.qi to every event's control set (ISA §4.7 `ctl w`).

`oracle_call`, `qexch`, `qexchm`, `qstore`, X and `xmask` are self-adjoint (ISA §5.3 adjoint table); `adj(f)` generates f from the current classical state and applies the adjoint of the event list; `compute` reuses the recording E_f for its uncompute, so masks and history match exactly.

**TDL-7 Workspace and declared outcomes.** Non-fault workspace, including temporary Co conditions and slice data, MUST be cleaned by the adjoint of its exact computing sequence before the invocation returns; `compute` f may retain it only until adjoint(E_f).
It is never implicitly made an output or measured.
Predicate and parameter computation are part of TDL-5(b)'s total-bijection check.
An uncleanable non-bijective coherent overwrite follows TDL-5(d), as ratified E3 requires; an out-of-place oracle or compute/use/uncompute retains that computation.
Per-slice codes and Φ are retained fault outcomes with TDL-8 lifetime, not incidental workspace.
Continuation flags, per-iteration conditions and preserved trajectory records are control workspace, including in a standalone adjoint; declaring compiler outputs does not exempt them.
Intentional deferred-measurement records (§7.5a) are separate channel outputs retained until their declared observation boundary, never a cleanup substitute.
**TDL-8 Faults.** NS §4.2: "a quantum action has no fault outcome of its own: any fallible computation it needs is a lifted oracle it calls, whose fault register it declares among its outputs".

Every slice invocation k gets a fresh 4-wire fault register f_k; the uncomputing invocation uses a second fresh register f′_k, which is then cleaned by `qxor f_k f′_k` (both hold the same code) and freed, so f_k holds the slice's code and is retained (TDL-7).

At the end of the invocation a runtime combine oracle `@firstfault` (§16.5) XORs the first nonzero code of f_1, …, f_K in event order (including generation-budget and virtual-device fault registers, not just slice codes) into the action's **declared fault register** Φ: the budget record's `fault` field (§9.1), or, when that is null, a register the plugin allocates and retains (TDL-7); f_k, compute copies g_k and a plugin-allocated Φ are declared fault outputs owned by CC.
They are exempt from invocation T-LEAK and are neither measured nor freed at invocation return or device-entry return.
No f_k is freed by firstfault. adjoint(E_f) reuses the same f_k wires (f9 in tdl-d); a cleaned f_k may be freed after that reuse.

The CC epilogue means program end: copy successive chunks of at most 128 bits of each remaining declared output into fresh non-view registers and measure those copies (ISA measure consumes the copies).
The original output wires now hold the known basis outcome and remain live for correction and clean free.
Report the invocation's combined Φ statistics (deduplicate correlated code copies, do not sum their rates), apply outcome-conditioned X corrections and free clean.
Caller-supplied Φ remains caller-owned under §6.6.
The certificate reports the rate (`fault_rate`, ISA §12.3).
On a faulting basis input a slice's payload is the canonical 0 (ISA §5.2).
Every event consuming a fallible slice result is additionally predicated on that slice's code being zero; if multiple results are required, all their codes must be zero.
This includes xchg, negative branch predicates and dependent slices: failure selects neither arm.
Success flags are computed reversibly from retained codes, kept until their last dependent use, then uncomputed.
These predicates do not gate the producing slice's compute/uncompute or fault collection.
Thus failed results leave dependent arena writes and gates unchanged.
A nonzero rate is a reported quantity (NS §4.2), not an error.
**TDL-9 Budget.** Generation G receives its own full region budget.
Before each executed materialised LLVM instruction other than phi/debug/mark it checks and consumes one step; heap and depth are checked before mutation.
Exhaustion is invocation failure, not a source leak.
No further source instruction executes.

Compiler finalisation runs without consuming the exhausted generation budget: before applying any recorded event, discard the failed invocation's speculative views and recorders, cancel all invocation-owned provisional allocations (including nested ones), preserve foreign handles, and emit only the corresponding declared fault event under the invocation/path controls.
Failed gen(f) does not run use; failure of either compute part cancels the still-unapplied composite.
Normal T-LEAK checks apply only to successfully completed source generation.
Nested G execution consumes the enclosing remaining generation limits as well as its own limits, so nesting cannot evade a finite bound.
Classical twins charge their executed instructions.
Compilation never runs G to completion to discover an event list: G is a bounded CC routine executed at invocation.
Every slice invocation's token comes from the region-entry marker's budget record, each field completed from the budget table (§9); each slice gets the full record (outline E2).
Exhaustion is that slice's `FAULT_BUDGET_*` and reaches TDL-8.
**TDL-10 Co control of quantum operations and stores.**

A marker call or outliving store that is control-dependent on a Co branch, or a marker call with a Co index or op code: a slice invocation computes the condition (and the index or code) into fresh wires; the event is issued under `qpred` of the condition wire, once per member of the index or code dispatch domain under the predicate "value = member" (ISA §3.5, §4.6); then the wires are uncomputed.
A Co rotation angle is predicated per value when its value set is finite.
Otherwise it is `BD-E-COHERENT-ANGLE`: NS promises predication, not superposed parameters, and ISA §3.1 "angles are literals or classical arguments fixed at region entry".

A loop whose trip count is Co is unrolled in the event list up to N = the `steps` field of the budget record: iteration i is predicated on the flag c_i (c_1 = the first continuation condition, c_{i+1} = c_i ∧ condition_i, computed by `ccx` into fresh wires).
Flags c_i, per-iteration conditions and preserved trajectory records are control workspace subject to TDL-7: clean them within their dependency-validity windows and before successful action return.
For preserved inputs compute bounded conditions out of place, apply the controlled bodies, then reverse their exact computing slices.

For overwritten inputs the complete bounded transition must meet TDL-5(b)'s total- bijection and bounded-inverse obligation: use that inverse on a copy of the output to reconstruct the entry, recompute the forward trajectory on copies, erase the original control records against it, then reverse the reconstruction and its copies.
All these slices preserve their inputs; all trajectory workspace is restored.
In compute, history may instead survive through use and be cleaned by the matching adjoint(E_f), TDL-5(c).
A non-bijective data-only update follows the existing TDL-5(d), with out-of-place oracle and compute interfaces still available.
A Co trip count alone never rejects a loop.
No trip-count record is measured at program end.
A loop is a structured event; its adjoint is the special rule of §18.2, not flat ccx reversal; if c_{N+1} may be 1 the invocation records `FAULT_BUDGET_STEPS` under c_{N+1} into Φ.
G-14 (§25.3) is the efficient form.

A `qalloc`/`qborrow` whose n is Co allocates the maximum of n's value set, padded to its bound (NS §4.2: "an allocation whose size depends on a qubit is padded to its bound"); gates on wires at or beyond the run-time n are predicated off.
An unbounded value set is BLK-1 (§25.1).
**TDL-11 After the region.**
Code that reads an object whose state is Co, inside the closure of a later region entry, is part of that region's slices (TDL-3).
Code outside every generation that may load from, store to, free or otherwise release a may-Co object is compiled in two variants (Cl and Co signatures, §4.3), selected by the object's dynamic state.

Its Co variant at host or CC level traps (`T-TAINT-HOST`, fault code 4), and statically the plugin warns (`BD-W-TAINT-HOST`, naming `__bennett_observe`): NS §4.2, classical outputs of coherent memory leave only through measurement.

A CC store is legal after observation of every byte it writes; for a partial observation while K=Co, permit only the covered basis bytes, update their authoritative arena cells and shadow together and retain that coverage.
Unobserved Co bytes still trap.
Release requires full restoration/dematerialisation as TDL-2 states, even inside a generation; it never silently reuses dirty cells.
`__bennett_observe(p, len)` observes successive chunks of at most sixteen bytes: copy each chunk's cells into a fresh non-view register of at most 128 wires and ISA `measure` it.
Sequential basis measurements preserve the joint distribution.
No whole arena register or slice view is measured.
Write the outcome into the shadow.
For partial observation of X leave its observed cells in |m⟩ and K(X)=Co: the arena stays authoritative.
When every byte of X is covered since its last write other than such a permitted CC covering store, XOR the whole measured X out of the arena and set K(X)=Cl.
Cl bytes are read from the shadow; M objects are dematerialised first. len=0 changes nothing.

**TDL-12 Effects in action regions.** Generations inherit the run's virtual device bindings, established by the CC launch stub from `--bennett-dev` (§19.9) using §8.3 model codes and widths; nested generations inherit the same bindings.
Marker signatures stay unchanged.
The build/launch record includes bindings, initial images, capacities and state registers.

Mutable model state (console buffer/length, clock counter, entropy cursor, block overlay and presence bits) is a declared mutable action interface, allocated in the arena at run entry and shared across invocations; entropy/disk images are preserved `in` registers.
The model's bounded undo log, containing saved overwritten bytes/presence bits needed for inversion, is explicit declared device state, not invocation workspace.
Initialisation is classical preparation outside control.
A bound operation is a controlled reversible transition of this state with the read values of §11.3.
Reads into program memory obey TDL-5; capacity exhaustion is a budget fault before mutation.
Slices compute parameters and validation, TDL-8 success predicates gate the permutation transition, and its adjoint restores state and cleans parameter workspace.
External effects wait for explicit CC observation of model state; adjoint/compute uncompute virtual transitions exactly.
CONSOLE appends without silently discarding action output; its finite capacity is a declared bound.
Clock, entropy and block use §11.3 values and cursor/overlay rules.
Only unbound/unmodelled operations or genuine host calls have `fault 8` and a trapped coverage line.
Release of outliving Co objects requires clean/restored state, not unconditional fault 8.
Oracle device state stays private under §11.3, with declared outputs under §8.6.
NS §4.2's effects table, made concrete.

statements.text: The four device models are the ISA's (ISA §7.3): `console`, `clock`, `entropy`, `block`.
H | – (host code calls its own libc; markers are never called from H) | real

CC | `hostcall bennett.dev.<model>.<op>` (ISA §10): a genuine host effect, since ISA `effect` is R-only (ISA §4.1); the host's reply carries the bytes a read returns | host functions by `hostcall` (§11.4)
R | ISA `effect <model>.<op>` on the effect tape, reversed by whole-run reversal (ISA §7.3, §10) | – (R makes no host calls)
L | the lifted device model of §11.3 over state bound by the descriptor (§8.3) | –
action regions | inherited virtual bindings: controlled reversible transitions (TDL-12); external effects deferred | unbound/unmodelled: F(8)
unmodelled | F(8) with a `trapped` coverage line (§4.5) | same

`__bennett_effect_<model>_<op>(…)` lowers to ISA `effect <model>.<op> …` with the operands in ISA §7.3 order: `console.write(ptr, len)`, `clock.read(ptr)`, `entropy.read(ptr, len)`, `block.read(sector, ptr)`, `block.write(sector, ptr)`.
A failing ISA validation (operands out of range, entropy tape exhausted) is the ISA's fault record (ISA §7.3, code 10 for entropy).
The driver declares the models in `devices.models` (ISA §9.1) and supplies `block_image` from `--bennett-disk=<file>` (§19.2).
`bennett-runtimes`' musl maps system calls onto the markers:
`write(1, …)`, `write(2, …)`, `writev` on fds 1 and 2 | `console.write`
`clock_gettime`, `gettimeofday`, `time` | `clock.read`: the 8-byte counter c; `CLOCK_REALTIME` and `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` both give tv_sec = c / 10^9, tv_nsec = c mod 10^9
`getrandom`, reads of `/dev/urandom` and `/dev/random` | `entropy.read`
block-device reads and writes (the platform's virtio-blk, §20.3) | `block.read`, `block.write`
files | a runtimes VFS over the block device, or over a data-image file system linked as a global
Device models beyond the four arrive with an ISA version (ISA §17 item 3, a mechanics deferral, §24): until then an effect on another device is `FAULT_EFFECT_UNMODELLED`.
In an L variant, an effect marker call becomes a call of the runtimes function `__bennett_dev_<model>_<op>` with the same operands.

These are ordinary C functions of `bennett-runtimes`, lifted like any code, over the **device state**: runtimes globals `__bennett_dev_<model>_*` that the oracle wrapper's prologue (§16.2) initialises from the descriptor's device bindings (§8.3) before the region function runs.
Their contract:

`entropy` | base = `lift.addr @e0`, size = 2^A bytes, pos = 0 | `read(p, len)`: if len > size − pos, `__bennett_nz_fault(10)` (`FAULT_ENTROPY_EXHAUSTED`); else copy [base + pos, base + pos + len) to p and pos += len

`block` | base = `lift.addr @k0`, nsect = 2^A′; an empty overlay | `read(s, p)`: the overlay's 512 bytes for sector s if present, else sector s of the region if s < nsect, else 512 zero bytes (ISA §7.3: absent sectors read as zero); `write(s, p)`: copy 512 bytes into the overlay entry for s (a heap allocation by `malloc`, lifted to `lift.alloc`)
`clock` | c = `value` | `read(p)`: store c (8 bytes, little-endian) at p, then c += 1

`console` | L = n(q)/8 (0 for a null q), a buffer of L bytes in the oracle's heap, n = 0 | `write(p, len)`: copy the first min(len, L − n) bytes to buffer[n…], n += that count; further bytes are discarded with the oracle's other writes
A model without a binding is unbound: every operation on it is `__bennett_nz_fault(8)` on the executions that reach it (NS §4.2).
The `entropy` fault code 10 in an oracle: ISA §4.2 admits `fault C` for every C < 2^F; ISA §5.4 labels code 10 "(R only)", which §25.2 records as a wording item.
The bound console buffer's bytes are output slices (§8.6).

A CC variant's call of an H function (§4.5 item 3) becomes `hostcall bennett.call/<h>` where `<h>` is the hex SHA-256 of the callee's symbol name: the argument block holds the scalar arguments (little-endian, in order) and, for each pointer argument whose pointee the analysis proves pointer-free (no slot holds a pointer atom, §5), the pointee's byte range as an (offset, length) pair and the bytes themselves.
The host-side stub calls the function on a copy, writes back the bytes of pointer arguments, and replies with the result and the written bytes.

A pointer argument whose pointee may contain pointers read by device code does not become a host call: the callee is **promoted** to a CC variant (§19.4; ISA-11 would let it stay native, an efficiency item).
Every service is declared in `devices.services` (ISA §9.1, §10).
ISA 0.8 does not specify which code a CC trap reports.
`__bennett_nz_fault(C)` in CC lowers to `hostcall bennett.fault` with a payload holding C, then `trap`; the service records C in the run's fault statistics.
A host call is forbidden in R and a generic R trap cannot preserve arbitrary C.
Typed R faults therefore have dependency blocker BLK-5 = ISA-7 (§25.1).

On ISA 0.8 a module has verdict blocked:BD-B-ISA7 if its device program contains an R-tier variant reached as an R entry: a reversible region candidate invoked outside generation, or the §19.2 whole-program R entry.
Every such variant has the §17.6 budget check, regardless of supplied run-time limits.
A reversible call treated as a direct call under §7.4 is not an R entry and does not by itself block.
Other rejection/blocker precedence remains §1.6.
The R blocker trap is generic ISA trap with no hostcall, reached only on executions that would report a typed fault (budget exhaustion, F(C), nz_fault(C)); all other executions are unaffected.
This fallback does not implement typed reporting.
Required operation: R fault C terminates with fault record code C, performs no subsequent source effect and preserves reversible prefix history.
No ISA 0.8 generic-trap path is claimed to implement this contract.
The R-tier console: a whole program in the reversible tier writes three bytes and returns 0; the tape holds one `console.write`; whole-run reversal restores the entry state:

```text blocker=effect-console-r
BD-B-ISA7 R entry: BLK-5 (ISA-7); mandatory pre-instruction typed fault 1 requires ISA 0.9 K5 fault C, exact terminal code, no subsequent effects, preserved reversible prefix
```

```text cc-run=effect-console-r
driver: --bennett-tier=reversible --bennett-entry=main
run: status=COMPLETED results=[INT(32):0] faults=[]
tape: console write args=[A(@msg), 3] bytes=68690a
reverse: status=REVERSED console=empty memory=entry
```
The same marker in a CC device function is a host effect:

```text cc-run=effect-console-cc
run: status=COMPLETED results=[] faults=[]
hostcall: service=bennett.dev.console.write payload=6f6b0a reply=empty
```
The ENTROPY-bound oracle of rung 8 is §16.8.
The normaliser rewrites every device variant (§4.3) and the initialisers of every global a device variant references; H variants are untouched.

It applies the rules of §12.2 in table order, each to the whole module before the next, with one exception: N33 is applied immediately before N32 so any floating-point instructions introduced by its expansions are processed by N32; own-format carrier calls and bit-exact reconstruction remain as specified in §13.4.
After N27 and N32, re-apply N22 to every instruction they created with an integer side wider than 128 bits.
Only width legalisation repeats; no other rule re-runs.
Width lowering may be fused with an expansion when the resulting canonical limb rows are identical.

The result is the **materialised module**: the reference semantics (§18), the lifting map (§16) and the native comparison build (§17.7) are all defined on it (NS §3.2: "the native comparison binary is built from that materialised bitcode").
**Naming.** A rule that introduces a value names it `%nz.<tag>.<r>`, where `<r>` is the name of the instruction being rewritten without its `%` (a number for an unnamed value).

For a rewritten instruction without a result (a `void` call, a `store`, an `invoke` of a `void` function), `<r>` is `<f>.<k>`: f the enclosing function's name and k the 0-based count, in instruction order, of the result-less instructions of f that the same rule rewrites.
A value introduced once per function is `%nz.<tag>.<f>`.
A constant global a rule needs is `@nz.<tag>.<f>.<r>`.
A declaration a rule needs is appended at the end of the module, and a global after the module's globals, in order of first use.
Each rule states its tags.
**Fault replacement F(C)** (§12.3) and the 35 rules.

statements.text: N13, N17, N18 and N20 are 0.1 ids whose rules are replaced (outline §12.2); they are kept as anchors.

N0 | the intrinsic families that LLVM defines by its own lowering passes: `llvm.coro.*`; `llvm.matrix.*`; `llvm.type.test`, `llvm.public.type.test`, `llvm.type.checked.load`, `llvm.type.checked.load.relative`, `llvm.icall.branch.funnel`; `llvm.instrprof.*`; `llvm.alloc.token.id`; `llvm.experimental.guard`, `llvm.experimental.widenable.condition` | the normaliser runs, only when the module contains one of them, the passes of the major in use, in this order: `coro-early`, `cgscc(coro-split)`, `coro-cleanup`; `lower-matrix-intrinsics`; `lowertypetests`; `instrprof`; `alloc-token`; `lower-guard-intrinsic`; `lower-widenable-condition` (which gives `true`).
Their output is then normalised by N1–N35

N1 | instruction flags `nsw`, `nuw`, `exact`, `inbounds`, `nusw`, `nneg`, `disjoint`, `samesign`, `inrange` (and `inrange(...)`) | removed: wrapping, inexact, out-of-bounds address arithmetic and the unflagged operation are defined
N2 | fast-math flags `nnan`, `ninf`, `nsz`, `arcp`, `contract`, `afn`, `reassoc`, `fast` | removed

N3 | instruction metadata other than `!dbg` (`!range`, `!nonnull`, `!noundef`, `!align`, `!dereferenceable`, `!dereferenceable_or_null`, `!tbaa`, `!tbaa.struct`, `!alias.scope`, `!noalias`, `!invariant.load`, `!invariant.group`, `!llvm.loop`, `!nontemporal`, `!prof`, `!alloc_token`, …) | removed; N3/N4-removed range information is ignored when computing §5 reference domains

N4 | attributes on device function definitions, their parameters and returns, and on every call site in a device function: `noundef`, `nonnull`, `range(...)`, `align` (except together with `byval`, `byref`, `sret`, `inalloca`, `preallocated`), `dereferenceable(...)`, `dereferenceable_or_null(...)`, `nofpclass(...)`, `noalias`, `nocapture`, `captures(...)`, parameter `readnone`/`readonly`/`writeonly`, `returned`, `writable`, `dead_on_unwind`, `initializes(...)`, `allocalign`, `allocptr`; function attributes `memory(...)`, `readnone`, `readonly`, `writeonly`, `argmemonly`, `inaccessiblememonly`, `inaccessiblemem_or_argmemonly`, `willreturn`, `mustprogress`, `nosync`, `nofree`, `norecurse`, `speculatable`, `personality` (after N28) | removed (attribute groups are rewritten; a group shared with an H function is first duplicated)

N5 | calls with no semantic effect: `llvm.assume`, `llvm.sideeffect`, `llvm.donothing`, `llvm.pseudoprobe`, `llvm.fake.use`, `llvm.dbg.*`, `llvm.experimental.noalias.scope.decl`, `llvm.codeview.annotation`, `llvm.var.annotation`, `llvm.reloc.none`, `llvm.prefetch`, `llvm.pcmarker`, `llvm.clear_cache`, `llvm.experimental.convergence.*`, `llvm.seh.*`, `llvm.xray.*`, `llvm.experimental.stackmap`, `llvm.eh.unwind.init`, `llvm.asan.check.memaccess`, `llvm.hwasan.check.memaccess*` | deleted (a token result is never used after deletion of its users) | | N5 | calls that return an operand: `llvm.expect`, `llvm.expect.with.probability`, `llvm.annotation`, `llvm.ptr.annotation`, `llvm.launder.invariant.group`, `llvm.strip.invariant.group`, `llvm.ssa.copy`, `llvm.arithmetic.fence`, `llvm.threadlocal.address`, `llvm.protected.field.ptr`, `llvm.ptrauth.sign`, `llvm.ptrauth.auth`, `llvm.ptrauth.resign`, `llvm.ptrauth.auth.with.pc.and.resign`, `llvm.ptrauth.strip` | every use replaced by operand 0; deleted.
*(non-normative)* Pointer authentication is a target feature with no device counterpart; the identity is one deterministic choice, made identically in both builds
N6 | `llvm.lifetime.start`, `llvm.lifetime.end`, `llvm.invariant.start`, `llvm.invariant.end` | deleted (a frame is live for its whole activation, §17.3)

N7 | `undef` and `poison` constants: whole operands, vector lanes, aggregate elements, `shufflevector` mask elements, global initialisers | the zero of the type: `0`, `+0.0`, `null`, `zeroinitializer` for a wholly undefined vector or aggregate; mask element `0`
N8 | `%x = freeze T v` | deleted; every use of `%x` replaced by v

N9 | `atomic` and `volatile` on loads and stores; `fence`; `atomicrmw`; `cmpxchg` | plain load/store; fence deleted; `atomicrmw op ptr p, T v` → `%nz.l.r = load T, ptr p`, `%nz.v.r = <op> T %nz.l.r, v` for `add`/`sub`/`and`/`or`/`xor` (for `xchg`: v; `min`/`max`/`umin`/`umax`: `icmp` + `select` named `%nz.k.r`, `%nz.v.r`; FP `fadd`/`fsub`: ordinary `fadd`/`fsub` then N32; `fmax`/`fmin`, `fmaximum`/`fminimum`, `fmaximumnum`/`fminimumnum`: respectively `llvm.maxnum`/`llvm.minnum`, `llvm.maximum`/`llvm.minimum`, `llvm.maximumnum`/`llvm.minimumnum` then N32; `nand`: `%nz.a.r = and T %nz.l.r, v`, then `%nz.v.r = xor T %nz.a.r, -1` (these two logical instructions, in this order, without flags); `uinc_wrap`: k=`icmp uge old,v`, i=`add old,1`, new=`select k,0,i`; `udec_wrap`: k=`icmp eq old,0`, g=`icmp ugt old,v`, w=`or k,g`, d=`sub old,1`, new=`select w,v,d`; `usub_cond`/`usub_sat`: k=`icmp uge old,v`, s=`sub old,v`, new=`select k,s,old` / `select k,s,0`. Names are `%nz.{k,i,v}.r`, `%nz.{k,g,w,d,v}.r` and `%nz.{k,s,v}.r` respectively, all arithmetic at T without overflow flags), `store T %nz.v.r, ptr p`, uses of `%r` → `%nz.l.r`; `cmpxchg ptr p, T c, T n` → `%nz.l.r = load`, `%nz.e.r = icmp eq T %nz.l.r, c`, `%nz.s.r = select i1 %nz.e.r, T n, T %nz.l.r`, `store T %nz.s.r, ptr p`, `%nz.a.r = insertvalue { T, i1 } zeroinitializer, T %nz.l.r, 0`, `%r = insertvalue { T, i1 } %nz.a.r, i1 %nz.e.r, 1` (single-thread assumption, recorded in the certificate, §24 D24).
Volatile accesses in platform-profile code are first routed by N35 (§20.3)

N10 | `llvm.is.constant.*` | `false` | | N10 | `llvm.objectsize.*(p, min, nullunknown, dynamic)` | `-1` (all ones) if `min` is `false`, else `0` | | N10 | `llvm.allow.runtime.check`, `llvm.allow.ubsan.check` | `true` (checks stay; a failing check is a fault) | | N10 | `llvm.allow.sanitize.address`, `.hwaddress`, `.memory`, `.thread` | `false` (no sanitizer runtime exists in either build) | | N10 | `llvm.get.dynamic.area.offset` | `0` | | N10 | `llvm.vscale` | the constant V of §12.5

N11 | calls of `llvm.trap`, `llvm.debugtrap`, `llvm.ubsantrap`, `llvm.looptrap` | F(4) | | N11 | `llvm.cond.loop(c)` | the block is split after the call; `br i1 c, label %nz.spin.<f>.<k>, label <rest>`; the new block `nz.spin.<f>.<k>` is `br label %nz.spin.<f>.<k>` (the infinite loop LangRef defines; budgets bound it, §9)
N12 | `llvm.abs.*(x, i1 true)`, `llvm.ctlz.*(x, i1 true)`, `llvm.cttz.*(x, i1 true)` | the flag becomes `i1 false`
N13 | (0.1: `memcpy` → `memmove`) | replaced by N26

N14 | `%r = shl/lshr/ashr iW a, b` with b not a constant | `%nz.c.r = icmp uge iW b, W`; `%nz.s.r = <op> iW a, b`; `%r = select i1 %nz.c.r, iW 0, iW %nz.s.r` (every shift by ≥ W gives 0, as the ISA's shifts do, ISA §4.1) | | N14 | the same with b a constant ≥ W | every use of `%r` replaced by `0`; deleted
N15 | `extractelement`/`insertelement` with any integer index i on L lanes | interpret iK index i as unsigned, including negative spellings.
A constant i<L is left for N21’s in-range lane renaming.
A constant i>=L replaces all result uses by the zero element (extract) or the unchanged input vector (insert), then deletes the instruction.

For a non-constant index: let W=max(K,⌈log2(L+1)⌉), zero-extend to `%nz.i.r` when W>K (otherwise use i unchanged); `%nz.c.r = icmp uge iW wide_i, L` with exact L; `%nz.e.r = <the original instruction>`; `%r = select i1 %nz.c.r, T Z, T %nz.e.r` with Z = the zero element (extract) or the unchanged vector operand (insert)
N16 | `%r = call T @llvm.fmuladd.*(a, b, c)` | `%nz.m.r = fmul T a, b`; `%r = fadd T %nz.m.r, c` (no fusion; explicit `llvm.fma` keeps fusion through §13)
N17 | (0.1: FP formats and transcendentals → F(8)) | replaced by §13 (N32, N33): no floating-point construct faults
N18 | (0.1: external calls in oracle and reversible closures → F(8)) | replaced by §4.5: shims first; trapped only without bitcode
N19 | floating-point arithmetic, comparison and conversion of `float` and `double` | the soft-float rewrite of §13.1 (applied by N32)
N20 | (0.1: alloca + memset) | replaced by N24

N21 | **vector scalarisation**: every instruction of vector type, every vector intrinsic (`llvm.vector.*`, `llvm.experimental.vector.*`, `llvm.vp.*`, `llvm.experimental.vp.*`, `llvm.masked.*`, `llvm.stepvector`, `llvm.experimental.stepvector`, `llvm.get.active.lane.mask`, `llvm.experimental.get.vector.length`, `llvm.experimental.cttz.elts`, `llvm.vp.cttz.elts`, `llvm.loop.dependence.raw.mask`, `llvm.loop.dependence.war.mask`), vector parameters and results of internal device functions | per-lane scalar instructions in lane order, by the rules of §12.6

N22 | **wide integers and non-byte memory**: an integer type iN with N > 128 in an instruction; a load or store of iN with N not a multiple of 8 or of an aggregate type | iN with N > 128 becomes L = ⌈N/64⌉ i64 limbs (limb 0 the least significant; the top limb is i(N − 64(L−1))) with the expansions of §12.7; a load or store of iN with N mod 8 ≠ 0 becomes a load or store of i(8⌈N/8⌉) with a `trunc` after the load and a `zext` before the store (fixing LangRef's unspecified extra bits as zero); a load or store of an aggregate becomes one access per element in element order at its offset (`%nz.e<k>.<r>`)

N24 | **allocas → shadow stack**: every `alloca`; `llvm.stacksave`, `llvm.stackrestore`; `llvm.frameaddress`, `llvm.sponentry`, `llvm.addressofreturnaddress`, `llvm.stackaddress`, `llvm.returnaddress`, `llvm.swift.async.context.addr`, `llvm.localescape`, `llvm.localrecover`, `llvm.localaddress`, `llvm.eh.recoverfp`, `llvm.eh.dwarf.cfa`; `llvm.structured.alloca` | §17.3

N25 | `byval`, `inalloca` and `preallocated` arguments; `llvm.call.preallocated.*`; aggregate returns wider than 128 bits | an explicit caller copy into a shadow-stack slot of the caller's frame (`%nz.bv<j>.<r>` for argument j) passed as a plain `ptr`, and the attribute removed from the callee and the call; a return of a first-class aggregate wider than 128 bits is demoted to a hidden first parameter `ptr %nz.ret` in which the callee stores the value (`sret` semantics)

N26 | **memory intrinsics**: `llvm.memcpy.*`, `llvm.memcpy.inline.*`, `llvm.memmove.*`, `llvm.memset.*`, `llvm.memset.inline.*`, `llvm.memcpy/memmove/memset.element.unordered.atomic.*`, `llvm.experimental.memset.pattern.*` | `call void @__bennett_rt_memmove(ptr d, ptr s, i64 n)`, `call void @__bennett_rt_memset(ptr d, i8 v, i64 n)` (the `i1` volatile flag and element-size operand dropped; a constant length becomes an `i64` constant; a narrower non-constant length is first `%nz.n.<r> = zext … to i64`); `memset.pattern(d, v: T, count)` → a loop storing v at d + i·size(T) for i < count (blocks `nz.mp.<r>.*`)
N27 | **integer intrinsics** | the fixed expansions of §12.8
N28 | **unwinding: explicit propagation** | §14.4
N29 | **setjmp/longjmp** | §14.5
